raw_response.conclusion: Plan B is provisionally preferable because it avoids Mira’s decisive, non-consensual loss while imposing only moderate uncooled discomfort on eight households and leaves Jo uncooled. Whether Jo’s complaint can outweigh the many moderate complaints that arise under C remains unsettled, so B is presently the uniquely defensible option among the settled comparisons, with an open question relative to C.
raw_response.strongest_objection: Jo faces the greatest heat exposure and could reasonably reject any plan that still leaves her unprotected when an available alternative (C) would relieve her without imposing a comparably severe uncon-sented burden on anyone.
raw_response.answer_to_objection: Under Plan C twenty households—including vulnerable members—also remain uncooled, and Sal incurs an income loss even if consented. Given uncertainty whether Jo’s single severe burden reasonably outweighs the many moderate burdens on others, rejecting C is at least as reasonable as Jo’s rejection of B, leaving the comparison unresolved rather than decisively favoring C.
raw_response.reversal_condition: If further facts showed that the heat risk to Jo was life-threatening while the other households could cope safely without cooling, Jo’s complaint would become decisively stronger and would likely justify choosing Plan C.
residual_disagreement: Severity of Jo’s exposure vs. cumulative burden on uncooled households
Whether Sal’s consent fully answers distributive concern for his income loss

paper_attribution.title: A Contractualist Argumentation Framework for Moral Decision-Making

evidence.value: During a heat wave, a council has funds for one of three technically feasible cooling plans. Plan A cools twenty households but requires demolishing Mira's occupied home, leaving her without housing; she refuses. Plan B cools twelve of those same households and displaces nobody. Plan C cools Jo's home, which has the greatest heat exposure of any home in this case, but requires closing Sal's only shop for eight weeks without compensation, depriving Sal of income during that period. Sal freely agrees to that closure after being informed of those consequences, without pressure. Jo's home is not cooled by A or B. Mira, Jo, and Sal are not members of the twenty households. No additional cooling, relocation, or compensation plan is available in this exercise. The text stipulates these effects, not total welfare scores or a ranking of whose overall position is worst. Which plan should the council adopt?
